sources.citation: RAVEL authored premises and conventions; license: Apache-2.0. External primary references are locator-only in each registry row.

nodes.statement: For an on-shell two-body decay use the complete amplitude and Lorentz-invariant phase space, average over initial spin when appropriate and sum final states. An identical-final-state symmetry factor belongs to the final-state phase space, not to identical incoming beams.
nodes.applicability: Review this convention in the stated process, observable, phase-space domain and perturbative order; retrieval does not establish applicability.

evidence.locator: RAVEL authored convention conv:two-body-width; primary references: Phys. Rev. D 110, 030001; review Kinematics, phase space and cross sections

obligations.description: Check masses, units, spin sums or averages and symmetry factors using the supplied amplitude.

nodes.statement: Small width relative to mass is a necessary guide, not a sufficient error bound for narrow-width factorization. Thresholds, cuts, off-shell tails and interference can spoil a rate-times-branching approximation even for a narrow state.
nodes.applicability: Review this convention in the stated process, observable, phase-space domain and perturbative order; retrieval does not establish applicability.

evidence.locator: RAVEL authored convention conv:narrow-width; primary references: arXiv:1206.4803, off-shell effects and signal-background interference; Phys. Rev. D 110, 030001; review Kinematics, phase space and cross sections

obligations.description: Compare the full prediction with factorization in the actual fiducial domain; use no universal width-to-mass pass threshold.

nodes.statement: At energies large compared with the gauge-boson mass, longitudinal-vector amplitudes relate to Goldstone amplitudes with convention-dependent phases and perturbative factors, plus power corrections. Mixing angles, field normalization and vertex signs must be fixed before comparing couplings.
nodes.applicability: Review this convention in the stated process, observable, phase-space domain and perturbative order; retrieval does not establish applicability.

evidence.locator: RAVEL authored convention conv:goldstone-equivalence; primary references: Phys. Rev. D 10 (1974) 1145; doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.10.1145; arXiv:1108.2040, model conventions and coupling orders

obligations.description: State energy hierarchy, gauge, field and coupling conventions and perturbative order before using equivalence or comparing model amplitudes.

nodes.statement: An EFT prediction requires a declared power counting, operator basis and truncation order. The relevant hard invariants and coupling expansion determine validity; a hadron collider beam energy alone is not the expansion parameter for each event.
nodes.applicability: Review this convention in the stated process, observable, phase-space domain and perturbative order; retrieval does not establish applicability.

evidence.locator: RAVEL authored convention conv:eft-validity; primary references: arXiv:1706.08945, power counting and EFT validity

obligations.description: Compare relevant partonic invariants with the stated validity scale and test sensitivity to truncation; do not infer a universal cutoff without model input.
